content:
For many people, their place of worship and faith community is central to life. Arthritis and frailty can make getting there and taking part harder.

This guide offers practical ideas for staying connected to a faith community. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Common barriers

  • Steps, uneven paths and distance from parking.
  • Long periods of standing, kneeling or sitting on hard or floor seating.
  • Cold buildings, which can worsen stiffness.
  • Getting there, especially in the evening or in winter.

Practical ideas

  • Ask leaders about step-free access, rails, accessible toilets and parking.
  • Ask for a chair with arms, or bring a cushion.
  • Sit near the door or aisle so you can move or leave easily.
  • Ask about lifts from other members or community transport.
  • Join online or broadcast services on difficult days.

Spiritual care and support

Many faith groups offer home visits and pastoral support. NHS hospitals and hospices have chaplaincy and spiritual care teams for people of all faiths and none. Ask the ward staff or care home how to contact them.

Faith practices and health

If fasting or other practices may affect your medicines or health, discuss this with your GP or pharmacist and your faith leader. Many traditions make allowances for illness and older age.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I ask my place of worship to make changes?

Yes. Many are happy to help when they know what is needed.

What if I can no longer attend?

Ask about home visits, phone contact and online services.

Sources and further reading

  • Age UK: Understanding frailty
  • Community Transport Association
  • NHS: Care services, equipment and care homes
